messages:
marie: Heads up — I'm prototyping an 'Inspector' quick-view for Console Analytics. Goal: when you're on a route page you can open a compact overlay showing active routing policy, quota headroom, and 1h/24h telemetry slices side-by-side. Question: how should filters/saved queries interact with this?

sam: Love the idea. Is this an overlay or a dedicated split pane? UX decision will affect how we treat persisted saved queries.

marie: Overlay for now (compact). Two main UX options I'm weighing: 1) Inspector applies ephemeral filters that do NOT mutate saved queries, or 2) Inspector can apply & save back as a scoped saved query (route-scoped).

liam: Ephemeral filters seems safer for exploration. Users often open things to debug and don't intend to create globals. Maybe show a subtle banner: "Ephemeral - not saved" with a save button.

anika: Agreed. UI pattern: small pills for current scope: [Route: /translate] [Model: open-10B] [Range: 1h]. Controls: "Apply saved query" (reads a saved query), "Inspect-only" (ephemeral), "Save as...". Keep microcopy clear.

marie: Implementation Q: our savedqueries API currently returns scope: "global" | "team" | "user" and a query blob. If we want route-scoped saved queries we can add a binding, but I'd rather avoid breaking changes. Thoughts?

sam: Non-breaking approach: add an optional "applies_to" array on saved query objects, listing route_ids or model_ids. Existing clients ignore it. Should be backwards compatible.

liam: Frontend needs a predictable contract though. For Inspector we'd want something like:
```json
{
  "route_id": "r-123",
  "model_variant": "open-10b-quant",
  "routing_policy": "primary->open-10b-quant,fallback->open-7b",
  "quotas": {"limit": "1M_tokens/month", "used": "420k"},
  "telemetry": {"p50": 82, "p95": 210, "qps": 12, "sample_rate": 0.25},
  "related_saved_queries": [{"id":"sq-9","label":"latency spikes","applies_to":["r-123"]}]
}
```
(This is just a sketch)

anika: Tiny but important: telemetry numbers must indicate sampling semantics. We changed sampling behavior for high-traffic routes in April; Inspector should show explicit sample_rate and a link to the raw metrics view.

juan: Ops/security note: If Inspector exposes any routing overrides (even preview toggles) we need RBAC gating + audit logs. We can't let everyone flip policy percent on prod.

marie: Agreed. Proposal: Inspector toggles are preview-only by default (local UI evaluation). If user tries "apply to route" require: 1) elevated permission, 2) a justification modal, 3) write to /audit/events with {actor, route_id, change, reason}. Reuse existing audit API.

sam: Also: when user hits "Save as..." from Inspector, default the saved query scope to "route" (if inspector opened from a route). That prevents cluttering team/global lists with route-specific debug queries. We should surface that default when saving.

anika: Edge cases: Private deployments (on-prem) might not store shared saved queries in the cloud. Inspector should gracefully degrade to "local-only" save and show an explanation tooltip.

liam: From FE/BE contract standpoint, can we standardize the inspector API to return a small, stable shape? Frontend will render columns: routing, quota, telemetry (p50/p95/qps), and saved queries list. If we keep keys flat it avoids extra parsing.

marie: +1. Also, rollout UX: Inspector should show model variant traffic split and a small expected latency delta for variants (based on recent samples). If a variant is <10% canary, show the fallback chain and estimated cost delta.

juan: Ops: add a throttle on "apply" calls and require a cool-down for repeated policy toggles. We borked a test once with rapid toggles.

deploy-bot: deploy started marie/console-inspector-api v0.3 -> staging at 2023-10-18T14:02Z :rocket:

marie: Nice. Next action items: sam to draft savedqueries "applies_to" patch for API, liam to spec FE contract (flat inspector payload), anika to wire the microcopy and save modal copy, juan to list RBAC/audit requirements. I'll follow up with a short prototype by end of week. :+1:

sam: I'll add the API RFC in the repo tonight.

liam: I'll post the FE mockups in #design once ready.

anika: Will create the copy doc and accessibility notes.

juan: I'll outline required audit fields and permission matrix.

marie: Thanks all!
